title: Review and Publish Results of Government's Measures to Reduce Socio-economic Inequality
what_it_is: Review and Publish Results of Government's Measures to Reduce Socio-economic Inequality

sections.label: Educational subsidies per student
sections.summary: A child in primary and secondary school receives about $11,000 in educational subsidies each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: A child who attends primary and secondary school receives around $11,000 in educational subsidies per year.

sections.label: Benefits versus taxes by income
sections.summary: Low-income households receive almost $4 of benefits per dollar of tax paid, middle-income almost $2.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: All in all, low-income households receive almost $4 of benefits for every dollar of tax paid, while the middle-income households receive almost $2 for every dollar of tax paid.

sections.label: Income growth and published reports
sections.summary: Lower-income real per capita household income grew close to 20% over five years, reported in Key Household Income Trends and SPOR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Our people have also seen good income growth with the lower income seeing their real per capita household income grow by close to 20% over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Such indicators are published every year in the Key Household Income Trends report by the Department of Statistics, and every two years in the biennial Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Review (SPOR) by the Ministry of Finance.

sections.label: Government commitment to progress
sections.summary: The Government is committed to the progress of its people, including reducing gaps among those in unequal situations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For this Government, our entire approach and, in fact, the raison d'être on which Singapore was founded on in 1965, was really to be a place where everybody can progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In fact, if we look at the proclamation of Singapore's Independence, it said that this would be a country founded on the principles of liberty and justice, and ever seeking the welfare and happiness of her people in a more just and equal society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What that means is that from Day 1, this Government is committed to the progress of its people, and that includes reducing the gap among people who have unequal situations.

sections.label: Reports publishing socio-economic indicators
sections.summary: Socio-economic indicators and outcomes are published yearly in Key Household Income Trends and shown in the SPOR report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The report is actually, as I indicated earlier, shown in the SPOR report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also publish the socio-economic indicators and outcomes every year in the Key Household Income Trends report by the Department of Statistics.
